verdicts.evidence: The spiked-cumulant model is implemented with visible spike u* and hidden v*; linear/PCA cosine theta_v sits at the d^{-1/2} floor (0.042, 0.031 at k*=2; 0.015, 0.006 at k*=3), confirming v* is invisible to PCA while the model structure matches the paper's description.

Real experiments at d=800 (below paper's d=2000) show ReLU recovers v* at k*=2 (theta_v 0.134–0.184 vs floor 0.035) while PCA/linear stay at floor, but k*=3 recovery is marginal (tanh 0.058, ~1.65× floor), only 2 k* values are tested, recovery of the visible spike u* is not reported, and no proof is attempted for this provable result.
No AMP experiments appear anywhere in the logbook; the executive summary explicitly lists AMP as part of the full replication that was not done.
No spherical gradient flow experiments are present; the logbook uses full-batch Adam instead, and the executive summary lists gradient-flow theory as not reproduced.

At k*=2, linear AE has lower test recon MSE (799.12 vs 800.11) yet higher downstream error (0.497 vs 0.451) and fails to recover v* (theta_v 0.031 vs 0.205), concretely demonstrating the misalignment phenomenon on the paper's synthetic model.

overall: The logbook provides concrete numerical evidence supporting the model structure (Claim 1) and the test-loss-misalignment phenomenon (Claim 5), primarily at k*=2 with d=800. It does not address AMP (Claim 3) or gradient flow (Claim 4) at all, and the nonlinear-recovery proof claim (Claim 2) is only partially supported by reduced-scale experiments with marginal k*=3 results.
